definitions.explanation: A thick, dark, rich soy sauce brewed mostly from soybeans with little or no wheat, made especially in the Chūbu region around Aichi. Often called たまり{醤油|じょうゆ}. Used for sashimi, glazes and simmered dishes.

examples.japanese: たまり{醤油|じょうゆ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: To eat it with tamari soy sauce.

examples.japanese: {愛知県|あいちけん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧たまり⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{濃|こ}い{味|あじ}→濃い味：21302_koiaji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|この}まれて→好む：02103_konomu⟧きた。
examples.english: In Aichi Prefecture, rich-tasting dishes made with tamari have long been popular.

notes:
Originally the liquid that collects (たまる) in a vat of fermenting miso.

TYPES:
- {濃口醤油|こいくちしょうゆ}: dark soy sauce — the everyday standard
- {薄口醤油|うすくちしょうゆ}: light-colored soy sauce, saltier, used in Kansai cooking
- たまり{醤油|じょうゆ}: thick, rich, low in wheat

Because it uses little or no wheat, tamari is often sold abroad as a wheat-free soy sauce; check the label, since not every brand is wheat-free.
